also: There is not one single Indian language, there are many. In Bengaluru and Karnataka, it is Kannada. You might hear other adjacent languages like Tulu, Konkani, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, etc.

Sandalwood is the Kannada movie world. It's more Shankar Nag, Vishnu Vardhan, Rajkumar, Puneeth Rajkumar, etc. Other languages have their own movie industries - Kollywood, Tollywood and Mollywood all run alongside it
Ragi mudde, bisi bele bath, chow-chow bath, ghee roast, filter kaapi in a steel tumbler-davara set
Pappu anna, bele saaru with rice, tovve - every part of Karnataka has its own lentil-and-rice combination

often: The Taj Mahal as the monument
also: Bangalore Palace's Tudor towers, Tipu Sultan's teakwood Summer Palace, Vidhana Soudha's granite legislature, the rock-cut Gavi Gangadhareshwara cave temple - four serious monuments, all inside city limits, no day trip required
Carnatic music, the veena, the mridangam, the nadaswaram. Hindustani music. Chowdiah Hall is a violin shaped building hosting kacheris

often: Kurtas and lehengas as the default "Indian dress"
also: Sarees and half-sarees are the draped everyday. You may also see panches (the lower wrap, kara at the hem) plus shalya (the shoulder cloth) - two pieces, not one. Stitched angi, kupasa and Kodagu kupya are local tailoring too.
More Deepavali here and Dasara (not Dusshera), Karaga, plus Ugadi, Onam and Pongal across the south
Not really, 5+ states here. Karnataka itself hsa diverse lifetyles - Coorg's estatae culture, coastal Mangalore lifestyle, Mysore's heritage, the jowar-rotti belt of North Karnataka

often: Rickshaws as the whole transport story
also: All still true, plenty of Auto Rajas, plus Namma Metro, app-based autos - worth trying a few modes, since the traffic stories aren't exaggerated either
